slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
Congratulations on completing all Level 2 courses! Now it's time for assessment. This exam covers all core knowledge from Level 2: Tuffeau geology, the Anjou-Saumur red wine group, the rosé spectrum, the Cabernet Franc triangle (Chinon / Bourgueil / Saumur-Champigny), the panorama of Touraine reds, and the influence of barrel type on winemaking style. Pass to unlock the door to Level 3 — Chenin Blanc and the world of flint.

📝 Assessment Scope

All 8 lessons of Level 2 (lo-l2-1 to lo-l2-8), covering 19 red/rosé AOCs

🎯 Number of Questions

5 comprehensive questions covering geology, varieties, pairing and barrel craft

🏆 Passing Standard

Answer 4 or more correctly (80%) to unlock Level 3
slides.1.title: Level 2 Comprehensive Assessment
slides.1.questions.0.question: What are the two most critical properties of Tuffeau (tuffaceous limestone)?
slides.1.questions.0.options.0: High iron content and reddish colour
slides.1.questions.0.options.1: Highly porous for excellent drainage + soft enough to excavate underground cave cellars
slides.1.questions.0.options.3: Rich in volcanic minerals + ideal for Gamay cultivation
slides.1.questions.0.explanation: Tuffeau is a highly porous white limestone that provides excellent drainage for vine roots, and its soft texture makes it easy to excavate underground caves (cave cellars), creating natural cellar environments at a constant 12–14°C. This is the defining geological feature of Anjou-Saumur.
slides.1.questions.1.question: Which is the most legendary estate of Saumur-Champigny?
slides.1.questions.1.options.1: Clos Rougeard (Foucault brothers, traditional large-oak-barrel ageing)
slides.1.questions.1.options.2: Domaine de Bellivière (Loir Valley natural wine)
slides.1.questions.1.explanation: Clos Rougeard (founded by the Foucault brothers, now owned by the Bouygues group) is the most legendary estate in Saumur-Champigny, celebrated for long ageing in ancient large oak barrels (foudres). Its flagship cuvée Le Bourg reaches €300–500+/bottle on the secondary market, earning the nickname 'the Romanée-Conti of the Loire'.
slides.1.questions.2.question: Why is Touraine-Noble-Joué one of France's most distinctive rosé AOCs?
slides.1.questions.2.options.0: It is the only Loire rosé permitted to add sugar
slides.1.questions.2.options.1: It mandates blending of three Pinot family varieties (Pinot Meunier + Pinot Gris + Pinot Noir)
slides.1.questions.2.options.2: It can only be produced once a year, harvested on a fixed date
slides.1.questions.2.options.3: It is France's only rosé AOC restricted solely to Cabernet Franc
slides.1.questions.2.explanation: Touraine-Noble-Joué mandates the blending of three Pinot family varieties (Pinot Meunier, Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir), creating a distinctive 'vin gris' (grey rosé) style with over 500 years of history — once the favourite table wine of French royalty in Touraine.
slides.1.questions.3.question: What is the most distinctive aromatic hallmark of Pineau d'Aunis, and in which sub-region is it mainly cultivated?
slides.1.questions.3.options.0: Honey and apricot; mainly in Vouvray
slides.1.questions.3.options.1: White pepper spice + violet; mainly in the Loir Valley (Coteaux-du-Loir) and Vendômois
slides.1.questions.3.options.2: Blackcurrant and cedar; mainly in Chinon
slides.1.questions.3.explanation: Pineau d'Aunis is celebrated for its white pepper spice and violet floral notes — the Loire's most distinctive indigenous variety. It is cultivated almost exclusively in the southern tributary Loir Valley (Coteaux-du-Loir) and Coteaux-du-Vendômois, and is rarely found anywhere else.
slides.1.questions.4.question: Among Chinon's three soil types, which best matches Rillettes de Tours — and why?
slides.1.questions.4.options.0: Clay-limestone plateau — firmest tannins, best complement to fat
slides.1.questions.4.options.1: Tuffeau slopes (coteau) — medium structure, ample acidity, minerality complements the cured pork
slides.1.questions.4.options.2: Gravel plains (graviers) — light and fresh, high acidity, best at cutting through fat
slides.1.questions.4.options.3: None of them — a white wine would be the better choice
slides.1.questions.4.explanation: Gravel plain (graviers) Chinon is the lightest and freshest, with the crispest acidity to cut through Rillettes' rich fat. When young, its strawberry and violet fruit creates an appealing sweet-savoury contrast with the cured pork. Tuffeau coteau Chinon also works well, but is better suited to richer meats such as roast lamb.
